person.name: Willie Roger Holder
person.description: Willie Roger Holder, a Black Panther–affiliated Vietnam veteran, hijacked Western Airlines Flight 701 on June 2, 1972 with his companion Catherine Marie Kerkow, framing the action as a protest demanding freedom for Angela Davis. The pair collected a $500,000 ransom and flew to Algeria, where they received political asylum, and later moved on to France. French police arrested the two in Paris on January 25, 1975, and Holder was held at Fleury-Mérogis Prison — about 128 days in all — while France weighed, and on April 7, 1975 refused, the American extradition request, treating the hijacking as politically motivated. On June 2, 1975 a Paris court convicted him over falsified passports and sentenced him to three months and fifteen days, releasing him for time served; he never attempted escape. In 1980 a French court convicted him of the hijacking itself and handed down a five-year suspended sentence. Holder returned to the United States on July 26, 1986, ending more than fourteen years in exile, and was held from that day in pretrial custody and then federal imprisonment until August 1989. He died on February 6, 2012 and is buried at Fort Rosecrans National Cemetery in San Diego.

cases.label: air piracy / exile / US custody
cases.charges: Air piracy — the June 2, 1972 hijacking of Western Airlines Flight 701
cases.sentence: In exile from June 3, 1972 to July 26, 1986 — political asylum in Algeria, then France. Returned to the United States on July 26, 1986 and was held from that day in pretrial custody and then federal imprisonment until August 1989.

cases.label: French custody 1975
cases.sentence: Three months and fifteen days, imposed by a Paris court on June 2, 1975, for falsified passports — released for time served, his detention since the January 25, 1975 arrest alongside Catherine Marie Kerkow having already run about 128 days. France had refused the American extradition request on April 7, 1975, treating the hijacking as politically motivated. He never attempted escape.

cases.label: French hijacking conviction 1980
cases.charges: Air piracy — tried in France for the 1972 hijacking
cases.sentence: Five years, suspended — imposed by a French court in 1980 for the hijacking itself; no time was served under it.
